The broader US-corridor pass found Qasim Naqvi: Slow Television at Roulette on November 18. Stage 1 admits the specific performance because Roulette commissioned two new works whose live architecture is unusually concrete: a solo modular-synthesizer study and a chamber work for piano, string trio, and three improvisers, with Caroline Davis, Grey Mcmurray, Scott Colberg, and members of the International Contemporary Ensemble. Naqvi also explicitly frames the music as a return, after almost a decade, to his open-form and graphic-notational language, and dedicates the pieces to Roulette. Stage 2 assigns A+. Naqvi's official site describes Slow Television as a new evening-length work intended to premiere at Roulette in fall 2026, making the context stronger than a routine presentation, but the scarcity challenge still resolves at A+: the current sources do not establish a terminal opportunity, farewell, or unique major-master context, and Roulette will livestream and archive the performance. A+ captures an event worth actively making room for without inflating every commissioned premiere into S. The recent/current RADAR intake remains weighted toward A and A+ with S/S+ reserved for narrower scarcity cases, so this grade is consistent with the current distribution sanity check rather than quota-driven.

events.factual_description: Roulette presents Qasim Naqvi: Slow Television on Wednesday, November 18, 2026 at 8:00 PM, with doors at 7:00 PM. Roulette lists $25 advance admission, $30 at the door, and $20 student/senior admission with ID. For this Roulette Commission, Naqvi will perform two new works: a solo study for modular synthesizer and a chamber work for piano, string trio, and three improvisers. The published lineup is Naqvi on modular synthesizer; Caroline Davis on alto saxophone; Grey Mcmurray on prepared acoustic and electric guitar; Scott Colberg on acoustic bass; and International Contemporary Ensemble members Josh Modney on violin, Miranda Cuckson on viola, Michael Nicholas on cello, and Erika Dohi on piano. Naqvi states that the evening continues an open-form and graphic-notational language he is revisiting after almost a decade, and the pieces are dedicated to Roulette. His official site separately describes Slow Television as a new evening-length work intended to premiere at Roulette in fall 2026. Roulette states that the November 18 performance will also be livestreamed free and archived.

en.why_it_matters: Naqvi is not simply bringing a modular-synth set to Roulette: the commission moves from a solo electronic study into a chamber piece where piano and strings meet three improvisers, including Caroline Davis's alto saxophone and Grey Mcmurray's prepared and electric guitar. The deeper thread is Naqvi's return to an open-form, graphic-notational language after almost a decade, giving the night a specific compositional problem to hear unfold in real time rather than just an experimental-music billing.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room if New York is already in play and let Roulette anchor the evening. From the DMV, I would pair the Brooklyn performance with another strong reason to be in the city rather than build a dedicated round trip around this single commission.
en.listen_before: No exact Apple Music item verified for this new commission; use Naqvi's recent modular and chamber work as orientation rather than treating an unverified release as required listening.

es.why_it_matters: Naqvi no llega simplemente con un set de sintetizador modular: el encargo pasa de un estudio electrónico en solitario a una pieza de cámara donde piano y cuerdas se cruzan con tres improvisadores, entre ellos el alto de Caroline Davis y la guitarra preparada y eléctrica de Grey Mcmurray. El hilo de fondo es el regreso de Naqvi, después de casi una década, a un lenguaje de forma abierta y notación gráfica; hay una pregunta compositiva concreta que escuchar resolverse en vivo, no sólo un cartel de música experimental.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente si Nueva York ya está en juego y dejaría que Roulette arme la noche. Desde el DMV, combinaría la función en Brooklyn con otra razón fuerte para estar en la ciudad en vez de hacer un viaje dedicado únicamente a este encargo.
es.listen_before: No quedó verificado un título exacto en Apple Music para este nuevo encargo; conviene usar el trabajo modular y de cámara reciente de Naqvi como orientación, sin inventar una escucha obligatoria.
